Disabling Cyclists with Impunity

By: Catherine Rice | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africa has the highest rate of alcohol related road deaths in the world.

Unique Selling Point:
The World Health Organisation says alcohol is a factor in almost 60% of road fatalities in the country. You'd think our traffic laws would be strictly enforced because of this alarming statistic. You'd be wrong.

Summary:
26 year old Dewald van der Westhuizen was cycling with his coach on December the 21st last year, when he was hit by an allegedly drunk driver. He was training for the Ironman, and it was just after 5 in the morning. CCTV footage captured the horrific incident, that left Dewald fighting for his life. After five surgeries, he is recovering well, but has vowed to never return to cycling on the road. The accused, Garth Pasha, was arrested three hours later. He was asleep at the wheel of his car. Blood on his car tied him to the earlier accident, and he was charged with driving under the influence, negligent driving, and attempted murder. His drivers licence was also revoked. But, in a shocking development his bail conditions were relaxed in May at the Simon's Town Magistrate's Court, and he was given his licence back. This, less than six months after the incident.

Further information:
Ren Brand is a 76 year old cyclist who has experienced the shortcomings in our justice system firsthand. He was in a hit and run in 2010 while he was cycling. The driver was sentenced to zero prison time. Ren lost his leg in that incident. In 2017, he was again cycling when he was hit by an alleged drunk driver. His prosthetic leg was damaged and had to be amputated further. In that incident, the accused received a sentence of community service. Why are drivers seemingly able to act with impunity? We speak to the Pedal Power Association about the failures of the justice system - how a clear message is not being sent to would be drunk drivers, and how if there is not more severe punishment, these accidents will continue unabated, leaving victims disabled, and in some cases dead.

Script:


UPSOUND Dewald Van Der Westhuizen Clip 0029 Time code 19:49 If there isn’t anyone on the road…its beautiful, it’s peaceful.

VO 1 It was just after sunrise in late December last year. Dewald van der Westhuizen had set out for a training ride on Cape Town’s False Bay Coast.

VO 2 But, just minutes later, the early morning tranquillity was shattered.

UPSOUND Dewald Van Der Westhuizen Time code 13:24 I didn’t hear the car coming, that’s how quick it is (clicks his finger). That’s the scary thing as a cyclist.

VO 3 The impact of the collision, caught on CCTV, was catastrophic, leaving him with what’s called a degloving injury… skin, tissue and muscle ripped from his leg.

UPSOUND Dewald Van Der Westhuizen Time code 02:03 I was cycling and then it was black, and as if I was just about to wake up and I thought this is kind of weird like why am I dreaming. I was just cycling. And when I opened my eyes that was when I was on the floor. 02:26 I looked up and saw the leg hanging open and then just put my head down and focussed on breathing.

VO 4 He would spend the next month in hospital, undergoing five operations on his leg.

VO 5 His injuries… life changing.

VO 6 This incident is another horrific reminder of the perils cyclists face on our roads… many ending even more tragically than Dewald’s. He didn’t know it at the time, but his ordeal would also be a reminder of the raw deal many cyclists believe they get from the country’s justice system.

Fade To Black

VO 7 Dewald’s girlfriend Darcy Le Roux was at his side during a painful recovery.

ERIN Clip CO107 / card 2 Time code 4:27 What’s been the hardest thing that you’ve seen him go through?

UPSOUND Darcy Le Roux / Dewald’s girlfriend CLIP 0031 Time code 04: not being able to do the things he used to like love doing.. your head is ready, but your body isn’t ..

VO 8 Despite his injuries, Dewald kept his sense of humour.

UPSOUND Darcy Le Roux / Dewald’s girlfriend. Time code It’s not nice to see anyone got through that. 05:It’s inspirational to see someone be able to still make jokes and still be themselves, but go through something so hectic.

NATSOUND Video clips of Dewald joking in hospital..him wiggling his toes, smiling in his hospital bed.

NATSOUND Dewald showing Erin the injury

VO 9 But, if Dewald imagined overcoming his horrific injuries would be his only challenge, he was wrong.

VO 10 The car was being driven by Garth Pasha, a member of the navy.

VO 11 Having fled the scene, he was arrested several hours later, asleep at the wheel, in a parking lot in Fish Hoek…damage to the car clearly visible. (photos of the car)

VO 12 Pasha was charged with reckless, negligent and drunk driving.. Leaving the scene of an accident…and attempted murder..

VO 13… charges he hasn’t yet pleaded to.

VO 14 He was released on bail of R5000 and his licence was revoked.

VO 15 But then, a twist that shocked not only Dewald and his family, but the broader Cape Town cycling community…

LINK Less than six months later, and despite opposition from the State, the court relaxed Pasha’s bail conditions and returned his licence. It’s a decision that has left Dewald’s family and the cycling community reeling.

VO 16 Despite being accused of almost killing a cyclist while driving at high speed and allegedly drunk, the court had allowed Garth Pasha back behind the wheel.

UPSOUND Neil Robinson / Pedal Power Association Clip 0061Time code 00:28 It sends the completely wrong message.UPSOUND Neil Robinson clip 0061 The cycling community is not blameless but they are outraged from a lack of results, it’s not the first, second, or hundredth or thousandth time this has happened.

VO 17 Neil Robinson is CEO of the Pedal Power Association and says cyclists’ lives are at risk every time they go for a ride, and when accidents happen there are rarely consequences.

UPSOUND Neil Robinson Clip 0060 Time code 00:11 I think South Africa is a lawless society bluntly put. Clip 0058 Time code 02:58 We have a country with rapes and murder and corruption like we have, cycling accidents seem to be the low end of the list unfortunately.

VO 18 Astonished that someone facing such serious charges could have their licence returned, we sought answers from the National Prosecuting Authority. In a WhatsApp the NPA confirmed it had opposed the application but accepts the court’s decision. (in text on screen)

ON SCREEN “..the State opposed the application by the accused to get his driver’s licence back but the court granted the application. We accepted the decision of the court”.

UPSOUND Darcy Le Roux Clip 0031 Time code: 06:14 It’s like very frustrating. I think to see it all. No one takes it seriously. Everyone is just acting like nothing has happened. Time code 06:36 It makes you just think no one cares.

VO 19 Darcy’s emotions are understandable. Not only is Pasha back on the roads, but there’s been an apparent lack of interest in properly investigating the case. A lawyer hired by Dewald’s family has sent several letters asking the police to obtain outstanding evidence.

VO 20 The investigating officer has also been told about other information that could be crucial to the case.

LINK: Darcy had gathered details from a witness who allegedly saw Pasha in a drunken state shortly before the accident and tried to stop him from driving. The police haven’t yet followed up.

VO 21 However, last week, the police agreed to meet the family’s lawyer. That meeting has yet to take place.

VO 22 In a whatsapp message, Pasha’s lawyer declined an interview as the case is still underway. .

ON SCREEN “Due to the fact that the investigation is still outstanding and the matter is still pending against my client, we have no comment at this stage”.

VO 23 Sadly, this isn’t an isolated case. For years, we’ve reported on sometimes deadly accidents involving cyclists across the country. All too often, those responsible evade justice or are handed lenient sentences.

UPSOUND Neil Robinson Clip 0060 Time code 03:36 If you look at the provinces, the regions, it happens everywhere. We get reports countrywide of things happening and very very few, miniscule few, actually getting prosecuted.

VO 24 In the past decade, he says about seven thousand accidents involving cyclists have been reported to the Pedal Power Association, but he believes the incidents are underreported.

UPSOUND Neil Clip 0059 Time code 01:32 We often don’t hear of people reporting these things, it comes by the back door, five or six months later when we hear a chap was killed or a woman hurt very badly because people just don’t bother anymore.

PAUSE

UPSOUND Ren Brand Clip 0002 Time code 16:15 There were so many things just really poorly investigated...Time code 16:48 Although we’d proved it was his car they couldn’t prove that he was in the car and he maintained his right to remain silent.

VO 25 Eighty three year old Ren Brand knows all too well what it’s like to live with a sense of injustice …

VO 26 Fourteen years ago he was hit by a car from behind while cycling on the famous Ou Kaapse Weg in Cape Town. As a result of the accident, his leg was amputated.

VO 27 The driver …who fled the scene… was later arrested. But, ultimately acquitted.

VO 28 Despite his devastating injuries, Ren returned to road cycling within a year.

VO 29 Shockingly, in 2017, he was hit by a motorist for a second time while cycling.. Again, the motorist fled the scene. Again…Ren had to endure a painful recovery.

VO 30 He hired an attorney to help ensure that perhaps this time there would be justice .

UPSOUND Ren Brand Clip 002 Time code 05:33 we managed to trace the guy which I don’t think would have happened otherwise. Time code 06:05 The sentence that he got had no real deterrent. They asked me in court, what I thought the accused’s sentence should be so I said the maximum. They said he’s not going to get that but we will give him community service

VO 31 He believes not much has changed within the justice system since his two cases.

UPSOUND Ren Brand / Cyclist Time code 13:07 People don’t go to prison, a lot of them get off, that’s all you want is justice and we’re finding we don’t get justice.

VO 32 For Dewald… he hopes that by speaking out, he can raise awareness.

VO 33 That ultimately…in his case… there might be justice. Garth Pasha, alleged to have driven the car that hit Dewald, will return to the Simon’s Town Magistrate’s Court later this month. It’s a chance for Dewald to face the man accused of nearly killing him.
